data.name: Vincent
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman name Vincius, which means 'conquering, tending to win'. In Christian tradition, Vincent is the name of several saints including Vincent de Paul and Vincent Ferrer.

data.numerology_meaning: Represents change, freedom, and personal expression. People with this life path number are often artistic, intuitive, and versatile.

in_hebrew.name: בינצנט
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בינצנט הוא שם שמקורו בלטינית, ומשמעותו 'שמע וקול, רענן, ומלא רעננה'. בעברית, שמע וקול מציין את השמעת הקול של האל, ורענן מציין את הגאולה. בצורתו האפריקאית, השם קשור לשם 'בינס'. באוריינטליזם, השם 'בינצנט' משמש לתאר אדם המושפע על ידי רוח הקודש. בכנסייה, השם 'בינצנט' קשור לרעננה, המסמלת את הגאולה

in_greek.name: Βίνσεντος
in_greek.meaning: ακούω και φωνή, ενηννοω και πλήρης εννοίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Βίνσεντος (Βίνσεντος) είναι όνομα που ερμηνεύεται ως 'ακούω και φωνή, ενηννοω και πλήρης εννοίας'. Στην αρχαία ελληνική, η φωνή (φωνή) αναφέρεται στη δύναμη του Θεού, ενώ η εννοια (εννοια) αναφέρεται στη σοφία και τη γνώση. Η εκκλησία χρησιμοποιεί το όνομα Βίνσεντος για να περιγράψει την ακρόαση της Θείας φωνής και την ενηντιότητα. Στη Βυζαντινή Αυτοκρατορία, ο Βίνσεντος ήταν ένα δημοφιλές όνομα για τους ιερείς. Σήμερα, το όνομα Βίνσεντος συνδέεται με την ιεραποστολή και την ακρόαση της Θείας φωνής

in_latin.name: Vincentius
in_latin.meaning: audio et vocem, enutrio et plenus intellectus
in_latin.long_meaning: Vincentius est nomen quod significat 'audio et vocem, enutrio et plenus intellectus'. In lingua latina, vox significat 'vox Dei', dum intellectus significat 'sapientia et scientia'. Ecclesia utilisat nomen Vincentius ut describeat audientiam Divinae vocis et intelligentiam. In Imperio Byzantino, Vincentius erat nomen populare pro sacerdotes. Hodie, nomen Vincentius connectitur cum evangelizatione et audientia Divinae vocis

in_english.name: Vincent
in_english.meaning: hear and voice, renew and full of understanding
in_english.long_meaning: Vincent is a name of Latin origin, meaning 'hear and voice, renew and full of understanding'. In English, to hear and voice refers to listening to God's voice, while renew and full of understanding refers to spiritual renewal and comprehension. In the Christian tradition, Vincent is associated with hearing the Divine voice and spiritual enlightenment. Saint Vincent of Saragossa, a 4th-century martyr, is the patron saint of wine growers, vintners, and people with hearing impairments. Today, the name Vincent is popular across various Christian cultures

biblical_reference.note: The name Vincent is not directly mentioned in the Bible, but its components 'vin' (wine) and 'cent' (hundred) have biblical references (e.g., Leviticus 10:9, John 2:1-11)

saint_reference.note: Saint Vincent of Saragossa (c. 235-304 AD) was a 4th-century martyr and the patron saint of wine growers, vintners, and people with hearing impairments

data.cultural_impact: The name Vincent has been popular in Western cultures since ancient Roman times, and its Christian associations have made it a name of reverence and honor within the faith. It has been used for multiple saints and has been featured in various works of art, literature, and music.
data.spiritual_significance: Vincent is a name that speaks to the power of the faith and the importance of victory over adversity. In Christian tradition, the name is associated with saints who have demonstrated strength, perseverance, and selflessness in the face of challenges. It serves as a reminder that, with God's help, we can conquer our own struggles and tend to the needs of others.

historical_references.reference: Saint Vincent of Saragossa, also known as Vincent the Deacon, was a Christian bishop and martyr in the late 3rd or early 4th century. He is said to have been born in Huesca, Spain, and was converted to Christianity by Pope Valerian I during his travels in the region. Vincent became a deacon and was appointed bishop of Saragossa. He was martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian in 304 AD. His feast day is celebrated on January 22.
historical_references.context: Christian martyr and bishop during Roman persecutions

historical_references.reference: Saint Vincent Ferrer (1350–1419) was a Valencian Dominican friar, preacher, and miracle worker. He is best known for his evangelization of Aragon, Catalonia, and parts of southern France. Vincent was born into a noble family and was educated in law before joining the Dominican Order. He was known for his eloquence and charisma, and his preaching drew large crowds. He also performed numerous miracles and was canonized in 1454. His feast day is celebrated on January 14.

modern_usage.modern_context: In the modern context, the name 'Vincent' is often associated with artistic expression and creativity. Vincent van Gogh, a famous Dutch painter, is one of the most iconic figures associated with the name. Today, individuals with the name 'Vincent' can be found on various social media platforms, such as Instagram, Pinterest, and DeviantArt, showcasing their own creative works and inspirations. The name has also become a symbol for artistic talent and innovation.

name_in_real_life.story: Thomas Vincent, a minister in London, United Kingdom, shares that their name Vincent meaning "Victorious" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Vincent means "conquering" or "victorious" in Latin, reflecting the belief in the Christian triumph over sin and death through faith and the power of God. It is also associated with Saint Vincent de Paul, known for his compassionate service to the poor and needy.
